questions.question: Describe the different types of grafting and their applications in horticulture.
questions.solution_html:
• • Approach grafting – scion and stock remain attached until union forms
  • • Cleft grafting – scion inserted into split stock
  • • Spice Grafting–It is a method of grafting by cutting the ends of the scion and stock completely
  • across and obliquely
  • • Whip and tongue grafting – interlocking cuts ensure strong union
  • • Side grafting – scion inserted into side of rootstock
  • • Propagation of fruit crops – widely used in mango, citrus, apple
  • • Combining desirable traits – disease resistance and high yield
  • • Disease resistance – resistant rootstock improves plant health
  • • Early bearing – grafted plants produce fruits faster
  • • Uniform plants – ensures consistency in orchard
  • Any of the above 4 types with explanations
questions.final_answer: Any of the above 4 types with explanations

questions.question: Give an essay on disease and pest management in Mango.
questions.solution_html:
• Give an essay on disease and pest management in Mango.
  • Important pests of mango are hoppers, stem borers, shoot midges, leaf-feeding insects, fruit flies
  • and mealy bugs. The common diseases are powdery mildew, anthracnose and dieback.
  • the following steps can be practiced to protect the orchard and trees
  •  Keep the orchard and tree surroundings clean by proper sanitary measures.
  •  Lime brushing on tree trunks will help to control some pests.
  •  Cuts and wounds on plant parts should be pasted with coal tar, used engine oil or
  • Bordeaux paste.
  •  Smoking in low intensities in the orchard during flowering season will reduce the number
  • of pests including hoppers.
  •  Spraying Pseudomonas fluorescens (10 g/litre) on trees before flowering and at flushing
  • times will improve the general health, flowering and resistance of the trees.
  •  To control fruit flies, collect and destroy attacked fruits that rot and drop down.
  •  Banana fruit traps can be used by mixing banana fruits (Palayanthodan) and jaggery (3–
  • 5%) poisoned with 2 ml malathion, and keeping them in hanging containers or using for
  • swabbing tree trunks at weekly intervals from flushing time onwards.
  •  Set up methyl euginol trap @ 10 nos/ha.
  •  Spathiphyllum (Peace Lily) plants can be planted as trap crop and the attracted insects
  • can be destroyed manually.
  •  To control stem borer, apply paste made of crude carbolic acid (130 ml), soft soap (1 kg)
  • and hot water (3.7 litres) to holes in the bark and plug the holes.
  •  Against sucking insects such as mealy bugs, thrips and mites, spray neem oil (0.5 to 1%)
  • – soap emulsion.
  •  Sticky bands or stem traps with mud slurry, jack latex, vaseline, grease, coal tar or gel
  • will prevent the upward movement of pests from soil.
  •  Red ants may become serious sometimes. If colonies are maintained at a moderate level
  • they help guard the trees from common insect pests. If severe, control can be attempted
  • by introducing predatory ant, Plagiolepis (Chonal ants), and by mechanical means such as
  • breaking ant nets, sprinkling wood ash or common salt pellets, and trapping ants.
  •  To control dieback, cut the affected twigs below the infected region and spray 1%
  • Bordeaux mixture.
